argument_review: A.1: locality in both entries uses supported cutoffs and extension by zero; first-jet dependence and real-tangent/complex-section conventions; full frame change and converse gluing.

A.2: complex general linear group established via matrices commuting with J and real smooth inversion; complex frame/associated charts supplied explicitly; bijection and global transport checked for rank zero and positive rank.
A.3: affine difference law is an endomorphism-valued one-form with the correct conjugation; converse and existence included.
B.1: tangent frame transition differentiated, both distinct bundle linearities identified, normalized vertical lift, reverse bilinearity-to-potential construction and horizontal graph checked.

B.2: arbitrary smooth maps, including critical points; derivative on the parameter space, chain rule and related-field identity; moving horizontal frame proves the exact inverse-transport difference quotient and its one-sided limits.
B.3: all second and first section derivative terms cancel in the commutator; tensorial curvature and arbitrary-rank pullback proved through naturality of forms.
C.1: dual and tensor derivatives glue; contractions cancel connection terms; symmetrizer and antisymmetrizer images are subbundles; Hom and conjugate bundle rules and induced transports checked.

C.2: real/Hermitian positive metrics from locally finite sums; complex Gram-Schmidt; global correction B=H^-1(nabla0 h)/2 and both self-adjoint terms; two directions of compatibility versus transport, with no Levi-Civita theorem assumed.
C.3: varying line metric, its unique compatible real potential, exact transport and orthonormal-frame check.
D.1-D.2: solder form on all frames, horizontal equivariant torsion, direct tensoriality and both structure identities with their correct wedge signs.

D.3-D.4: coordinate-independent tangent interchange, full torsion along critical maps, antisymmetrized coefficients, torsion removal without changing the velocity equation and a constant nonzero example.
E.1-E.2: affine Lie group and frame-bundle atlas constructed explicitly, rank-zero case, all generalized connection pairs and normalized bijection from complete local-potential gluing.
E.3: exact block curvature, connection-preserving linear-part map and onto images of both full and restricted holonomy using the same base loops.
F.1: associated affine evaluation, global inhomogeneous equation, integral development with the correct negative sign, uniqueness, corners and transport identities.
F.2: variable-origin gauge formula, parallel point fields, all flat Euclidean solutions and circle monodromy obstruction.
F.3: complete nilpotent/diagonal exercise, derivative contribution to changed curvature, endpoint frame factors and dual potential.
G.1: C1 transport extension supplies the C2 development derivative; affine parametrization distinguished from a straight image. Closed-loop affine pair and opposite convention derived explicitly.

G.2: tangent projection is proved metric and torsion-free before invoking exact earlier uniqueness. Latitude frame orientation, connection sign, inverse-velocity integral and affine fixed-centre sign computed. Negative c and zero c treated separately; uniqueness uses the full earlier circle period proof.
G.3: special trigonometric constants derived from the earlier exponential, polynomial factorization and positive square roots; both specified latitudes and equator computed.

H.1: nonlinear projection coordinate formula; differentiation at the zero section proves bilinearity; converse uses constant local sections and cutoffs. Complex case includes J as a separate parallelness requirement.

H.2: horizontal/vertical splitting gives the coframe; standard fields and equivariance derived. Flow-pullback differentiation fixes the bracket sign; structure forms give both bracket components and converse vanishing.

H.3: prescribed trivial-group counterexample and nonexistence of a unit-frame reduction verified. General metric-preserving equivalence explicitly assumes that the specified orthonormal locus is a smooth principal reduction.

H.4: derivation locality proved with cutoffs; integral Hadamard identity gives smooth vector coefficients. Both directions of the section-valued one-form formulation retain additivity and real tangent directions.
